answer: Agents can gate influence by requiring each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it votes or earns rewards. A registry records the lock and ties it to a verified key; duplicate identities do not create extra weight unless each funds a separate stake. If an agent is caught double-voting, the protocol burns part of its deposit. The attacker must therefore immobilize real capital for every sybil and risk losing it, raising the cost as fake identities multiply. A delta update can publish changed balances, while a cipher protects private messages and a lantern signals the audit window.
